newsitem.title: USA: Planet Hollywood, Saudi Prince in alliance.
newsitem.headline: Planet Hollywood, Saudi Prince in alliance.

text.p: Planet Hollywood International Inc. announced Wednesday a key franchising agreement with Saudi Prince Alwaleed Bin Talal Bin Abdulaziz Al Saud that would add 34 new Planet restaurants in 23 countries.
The company, which has movies and sports entertainment-based theme restaurants, also announced that its profits more than tripled in the first quarter.
Planet Hollywood's stock jumped $2.44 to $18.56 on the Nasdaq market.
The company said that Prince Alwaleed bought 1 percent of Planet Hollywood's outstanding common stock from the company as part of the alliance.
Planet Hollywood did not disclose the value of the deal but analyst said the prince agreed to buy the Planet Hollywood stake at $18 per share.
Prince Alwaleed said he planned to open Planet Hollywood units in Brussels, Athens, Cairo, Lisbon, Istanbul and Budapest, and to take an interest in the Beirut unit.
Prince Alwaleed also has rights to develop Planet Hollywood's new music concept Official All Star Cafe units, Planet Hollywood Superstores as well as future business opportunities, the company said.

"Planet Hollywood is a dynamic well managed company with exciting concepts that appeal to consumers in the Middle East and elsewhere around the world. I am pleased to participate in their continuing international expansion," the Saudi prince said.

Prince Alwaleed's previous international investments included interests in Citicorp, Saks Fifth Avenue, the Plaza Hotel in New York, the Four Seasons Hotel in London, the Disneyland theme park in Paris, the Canary Wharf real estate development in London. He recently acquired stakes in Trans World Airlines and Apple Computer.
PaineWebber in a research report, described Price Alwaleed as "an enormously successful bottom fishing investor ... in consumer brand names."
The prince "bought into Citicorp at the bottom" according to PaineWebber.
Wayne Daniels, an analyst for Schroder Wertheim said, "The agreement with the prince obviously bolsters confidence in the company's meeting its frachising goals. It is a positive."
Meanwhile Planet Hollywood said its first quarter earnings jumped to $10.5 million, or 10 cents a share, from year-earlier earnings of $3.3 million, or 4 cents a share.
Revenues rose 32 percent to $101.6 million from $77.0 million.
Analysts said growth in mechandise sales was the most significant factor contributing to the first quarter results.
Of the $101.6 million in revenues, they said that merchandise sales accounted for $37 million of the total.

The company said it opened four new Planet Hollywood units in the quarter, bringing the total number of restaurants to 57, including 36 company-owned units and 21 franchised units in 21 countries worldwide.
In addition to Planet Hollywood, the company has Official All Star Cafe, a sports-themed restaurant-merchandise store, and Marvel Mania, a comic book-themed restaurant-merchandise store.
